description:
World::canonical_activation_key_inner (src/compiler2/world.rs:2358) clones the InputDemand (Vecs of recursive DispatchDemand) because input_demand(&self) borrows all of World ahead of &mut self.types; the fields are disjoint. Types::activation_key_arrow (src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:1787-1789) then copies local, forwarded and returned with to_vec to build a KeyQuery, which is stored on a miss and thrown away on a hit.
Shape: read the demand through the field so the borrow splits from types. For the memo probe, a hit should allocate nothing: prefer an interned demand id as the key over a borrowed-key lookup; if neither is clean, land the world.rs half and report.
Heat: per call site per analysis round (prepare_function_call, jobs/semantic.rs:2245, from :1521 and :1694).

Method: .agent/strategies/ownership-shape.md. Change the signature and let cargo check enumerate dependents; resolve interleavings by compute-then-commit or a split borrow; stop and report if an Rc is the only move.
Signal: pure refactor. Full gate green; no golden, census or pin moves. Report the clone/to_vec count of each touched file before and after.
Sites were read at develop 8bf8775ae and not compiled; confirm each with cargo check before relying on it.
title: Activation-key derivation borrows the input demand
